heading: A single hidden state can predict tokens several positions ahead
definition: a single hidden state contains enough information to predict tokens several positions ahead.
summary: Several independent groups decoded tokens beyond the next one from a single hidden state. Success depends on the task and prediction distance; probes on general Pile text did not exceed a unigram baseline eight tokens ahead.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: R2. 10-100B: R2 for rhyme and English t+2, with a k=8 null on general text. <1B: ?. Toy: R0. >100B: none.
suggested_status.reason: Groups other than the original's (counts: versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0) decode tokens past the next one: arXiv:2407.02446#probe-pile-own-3, arXiv:2609.04708#R10 and arXiv:2605.07984#probe-qwen32. In arXiv:2609.04708, English uses t+2; French uses special alignment because l’ spans two tokens, with the state immediately before the lexical trigger, so a common t+2 offset from allomorph prediction is not established (arXiv:2609.04708#R15). counts: versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies = 12; versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. arXiv:2605.07984#pile-qwen32, arXiv:2605.07984#pile-gemma27 and arXiv:2605.07984#pile-llama70 find no decodability above the unigram baseline at k=8 on the Pile.
suggested_status.open_questions: A test on general text at N=1-3 in another family with a unigram baseline; offsets of 4-7; models above 100B; whether a single layer suffices.

source.title: Future Lens: Anticipating Subsequent Tokens from a Single Hidden State
source.authors: Koyena Pal; Jiuding Sun; Andrew Yuan; Byron C. Wallace; David Bau

original_result.setup: Pal et al. transplanted a single GPT-J-6B hidden state into learned or fixed prompts and compared linear prediction methods.
original_result.result: Learned prompts achieved 48.4%, 43.7%, and 46.9% future-token accuracy at prediction distances N=1, 2, and 3, respectively. Direct linear vocabulary prediction achieved 27.5%, 19.4%, and 14.7% at the corresponding distances.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Combined paragraph-boundary activations across all layers preserved information about the upcoming topic.
Probes predicted tokens up to three positions ahead, better for RLHF than Base.
Blocksworld probes decoded future colour decisions from a single hidden state.
A final-layer state encoded beliefs determining future-token distributions in a synthetic HMM.
Hidden-state probes predicted later content words and answer choices above random baselines.
Probes predicted post-reasoning answers early with small accuracy losses.
Paragraph-transition states revealed upcoming topic content above random baselines.
Numerical probes recovered predictive statistics more accurately than input baselines.
Late-layer states revealed upcoming phonological triggers across English, French, and Italian.
PersonaPlex states encoded upcoming response embeddings after receiving the turn-start token.
Hidden states revealed future rhyme words about eight tokens ahead.
Paragraph-boundary states revealed broad content of the upcoming paragraph.
Activation transplants recovered complex topics partially or failed to recover them.
Future-token decodability depended on continuation predictability and whose generations probes predicted.
Future-decision decoding weakened with distance and could reflect state encoding rather than planning.
Linear recovery of full belief geometry in RRXOR required concatenating layers.
Answer prediction weakened at early input positions and for longer outputs.
Paragraph probes recovered few specific details and little topic information before transitions.
Probes recovered decoded numbers less accurately than distribution means or medians.
Upcoming response embeddings became decodable only after the turn-start token was fed back.
Next-step answer decoding was low and varied with fine-tuning.
Eight-token probe accuracy on general text overlapped unigram baselines at every layer.
Upcoming-paragraph recovery weakened for specific details and before the paragraph boundary.

wording_issues.issue: Some associated results combine layers at one position. arXiv:2603.02913's main numeric-output probes concatenate 8 layers. In arXiv:2405.15943, full RRXOR belief-state geometry was linearly recoverable from concatenated layers but not individual layers; this does not establish absence of future-token information in individual layers. arXiv:2409.06328 uses all-layer transition-token transplantation in Gemma 2 9b to recover paragraph-level semantics, without testing single-layer future-token prediction. These multi-layer results do not establish the single-hidden-state claim.

Associated results use different targets: post-CoT answer classes in Llama3.1-8B (arXiv:2502.13329), paragraph topic in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (arXiv:2511.00180), and response embeddings in PersonaPlex (arXiv:2609.31588). PersonaPlex does not measure future-token identities or token distance. In the Mess3 toy transformer (arXiv:2405.15943), final-layer belief-state geometry is recovered; because belief states determine future-token distributions, this is observed indirect evidence, rather than a reported result of partial future-token recovery.

Exact-token offsets tested include N up to 3 in the original GPT-J-6B study, n=1-3 in Llama 2 7B Base and RLHF (arXiv:2407.02446), and English t+2 in arXiv:2609.04708. The latter's French examples require special alignment because Lucie's l’ spans two tokens; a common t+2 offset from allomorph prediction is not established. In arXiv:2605.07984, rhyme tokens about 8 tokens ahead are decodable in Qwen3-32B, Gemma-3-27B and Llama-3.1-70B, while general-text Pile tokens at k=8 do not exceed the unigram baseline. The rhyme probes establish decodability, not causal use.

Reported prediction performance varies by target and condition. Original GPT-J-6B learned-context accuracy at N=1, layer 14 is 23.3-52.1% depending on token category. In Blocksworld, maximum linear-probe accuracy is 0.51 (fraction) for predicting the step-6 decision from step 1 in full-parameter-fine-tuned Llama-2-7b-chat-hf, using correct six-block examples under teacher forcing; no chance baseline is stated, and action-step distance does not establish a token-horizon ceiling. For Qwen3-0.6B-Base on iGSM, next-step answer accuracy is 0.062 after standard SFT and 0.104 with masked pause tokens (fractions); no chance baseline is stated. For Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct paragraph recovery, moderate-depth detail preservation is 3% for TAE and 15% for Continuation, versus 17% for cheat-5 and 79% for regeneration; this measures detail preservation rather than exact-token accuracy.

method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2511.00180, Continuation ParaScope layer-scrubbing test on an unspecified 42-layer model: the cosine-similarity delta for future-paragraph content is below 0.05 with layers 0-25 and 0.15-0.25 with layers 25-35. Section 6.1 does not identify the model; this experiment cannot be attributed to the 28-layer Llama-3.2-3B. This measures paragraph semantics. Original arXiv:2311.04897: learned-prompt accuracy peaks at middle layer 14 (not in rows). arXiv:2502.13329: early layers give poor answer-probe consistency (not in rows).

On Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, the ParaScopes paper (arXiv:2511.00180) compares against random (cosine 0.20) and the LessWrong post against cheat-5 (0.44). These measure paragraph semantics rather than exact future tokens. The reader marked the paper's rows partial and the post's SONAR rows observed, which produces both conflict-index groups. arXiv:2605.07984: on Llama-3.1-70B, the Pile k=8 result shows no future-token decodability above the unigram baseline.

Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct paragraph recovery: TAE vs Continuation (arXiv:2511.00180) gives cosine 0.55 vs 0.43 and subject match 76% vs 43%; SONAR vs Continuation (lw:9NqgYesCutErskdmu) gives cosine 0.50 vs 0.33. arXiv:2603.02913, Appendix C.1 (comparison not in rows): factorised probes reduce MSE relative to vanilla MLP without log-scaling by 41%, 33% and 42% for greedy, mean and median targets, respectively. These probes recover numerical outputs and concatenate eight layers. Original GPT-J-6B at N=1: fixed-prompt accuracy 20.8%, against 23.3-52.1% for learned-context, depending on token category.

arXiv:2605.07984: in Qwen3-32B, Gemma-3-27B and Llama-3.1-70B, last-word and newline probes both decode the later rhyme token better than probes at subsequent generated positions; last-word probes peak earlier and decay later. This is not a newline-success versus last-word-failure contrast. Paragraph-topic recovery differs between pre-transition and transition tokens (arXiv:2511.00180: cosine similarity 0.12 before versus 0.48 at the transition); answer-probe consistency differs between early and final input tokens (arXiv:2502.13329). The latter concerns accessible answer-class prediction with these probes; Section 6's body names CSQA while its caption names CosmoQA.

Own vs other model's text (arXiv:2407.02446). Greedy vs mean MSE (arXiv:2603.02913): Llama-2-7B 0.015 vs 0.006. Original GPT-J-6B, N=1, layer 14: learned-context accuracy ranges from 23.3% to 52.1% by token category; calibrated accuracy is 26%, 57% and 77% for confidence groups 0-30%, 30-60% and 60-90%, respectively. arXiv:2605.07984: Gemma-3-27B decodes the rhyme token about 8 tokens ahead, while future-token decodability on the Pile at k=8 is absent above the unigram baseline.

Qwen3-0.6B-Base on iGSM (arXiv:2609.04489): base 0.075, standard SFT 0.062, masked pause 0.104, unmasked 0.094. Llama 2 7B (arXiv:2407.02446): RLHF scores above Base. Mess3 (arXiv:2405.15943): the geometry emerges over training.

Larger Llama3 models are consistently better (arXiv:2502.13329, no numbers in the text). In English allomorph contexts, arXiv:2609.04708 reports FutureLens top-5 agreement of about 90% at late-layer peaks in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Gemma-3-1b-it, versus 81.8% at the final layer in Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. French uses special alignment because Lucie tokenizes l’ as two tokens: the readout state is immediately before the lexical trigger, and a uniform t+2 offset from allomorph prediction is not established. arXiv:2605.07984: family and size matter; in Gemma-3-27B the handoff comes around layer 30. Character-choice F1 rises with size, slope 0.019 (arXiv:2502.06258, not in rows).
